content: Miconazole is an antifungal medication classified as an azole antifungal drug. It is used to treat fungal infections in the mouth or throat, such as oral thrush. Instructions for Use: 1. Preparation: Before starting miconazole or refilling your prescription, read the Patient Information Leaflet and Instructions for Use provided by your pharmacist. Follow your doctor’s directions carefully. 2. Dosage: This medication is typically used once daily in the morning, after brushing your teeth. 3. Application: Identify the placement area in your mouth. The tablet should be placed on the upper gum, just above either the left or right incisor tooth. The incisors are the teeth located immediately to the left and right of your two front teeth. With dry hands, place one tablet in your mouth with the rounded side facing your gum. Gently press it into place. Remove your hand from your mouth and apply slight pressure with your finger on the outside of your upper lip for 30 seconds. This ensures the tablet adheres to your gum. 4. Dissolution: Leave the tablet in place until it dissolves completely, which usually takes 6 hours or longer. You may eat and drink while using this medication. 5. Precautions: Do not crush, chew, or swallow the tablet. After brushing your teeth, rinsing your mouth, eating, or drinking, check to ensure the tablet is still in place. Before applying the next dose, remove any remaining pieces of the previous tablet. It is acceptable if the tablet adheres to your gum, lip, or cheek. If the tablet does not stick or falls off within the first 6 hours, reapply it as directed. If it still does not adhere, replace it with a new tablet. However, if the tablet falls off or is accidentally swallowed after 6 hours, do not apply a new dose. Treatment Duration: Antifungal medications work best when the drug concentration in your body remains constant. Continue using this medication for the full prescribed duration, even if symptoms improve after a few days. Side Effects: Common side effects may include discomfort, sores, taste changes, or irritation/pain in the mouth. Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, abdominal pain, or headache may also occur. Serious allergic reactions are rare but can occur. Seek immediate medical attention if you experience symptoms such as rash, itching/swelling (especially of the face/tongue/throat), severe dizziness, or trouble breathing. Precautions: Inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to miconazole or any other substances. This product may contain inactive ingredients (e.g., milk protein concentrate) that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. During pregnancy, use this medication only if clearly needed. It is unknown whether this drug passes into breast milk. Consult your doctor before breastfeeding. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription/nonprescription drugs and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Overdose: In the event of an overdose with serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Missed Dose: If you miss a dose, use it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Storage: Store this medication at room temperature, away from moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Important Notes: This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs.
